To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expansion of the pulmonary capillary network in adult rat lung is achieved by a combination of processes, including the formation of interluminal structures, intussusceptive growth, and lumen subdivision by the formation of loop structures.

pulmonary capillary segments remodel in adult lung by expansion and increased numbers, and that the expansion of capillary segments and their increased number occur by the formation and growth of interluminal structures, and by intussusception.
pulmonary capillaries remodel in response to injury in high oxygen by the processes of ILS formation, sheet infolding, and intussusception.
In summary, our research is concerned with
mechanisms underlying the formation of a pulmonary capillary network in adult lung, which is essential to maintain gas exchange.
the mechanisms by which the pulmonary capillary network expands and remodels during the process of recovery from hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction.
the mechanisms of growth of a capillary network in adult lung.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mechanisms involved in the growth and remodeling of pulmonary capillaries include: (a) endothelial cell proliferation and expansion; (b) formation of ILS by intussusception and by intussuspective microvascular growth; (c) formation of loops by infolding of the endothelial cell–epithelial cell sheet into the capillary lumen.

the mechanisms of segmental growth in adult lung are similar to those of growth in the embryo, but with the added complexity of the presence of an epithelium and a basement membrane, which is not the case during development.

the mechanisms of capillary growth in lung are not limited to sprouting angiogenesis and IMG, but also include endothelial sheet infolding and extension of endothelial processes to bridge the capillary lumen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pulmonary capillary growth in adult lung occurs by a combination of processes, including IMG, that increase the density of segments and their length.
the expansion of pulmonary capillary networks in adult lungs is achieved by the combined action of ILS formation and IMG.
capillary growth in adult lung is a process of lumen subdivision by sheet infolding and by IMG, with each process being driven by endothelial cell extension and by the formation and growth of ILSs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expansion of capillary segments and increased segment density in adult lung is a consequence of endothelial–epidthelial infolding, loop formation, and ILS formation.
ILSs are a novel form of capillary remodeling that may be a general mechanism in the expansion of capillary segments.
the pulmonary capillary network in adult lung can expand in size and density in response to injury by a combination of processes that include ILS formation, lumen subdivision, and IMG.
